comparisons.peer_topic: Export Control Licensing Requirements for Specific Regions and Products
comparisons.peer_summary: The U.S. government has imposed various export licensing requirements on Nvidia's products, initially affecting A100 and H100 chips to China, Russia, and the Middle East in 2023, and later expanding in October 2023 to cover products exceeding certain performance thresholds shipped to China, the Middle East, and other designated Country Groups.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVDA disclose risks related to U.S. government trade regulations and export controls impacting their product sales. MU states that 'increased tariffs imposed by the countries in which our products are sold can increase the cost of our product to our customers,' focusing on the cost impact of tariffs. In contrast, NVDA details specific U.S. government licensing requirements imposed on exports to China, Russia, and specific Middle Eastern countries, noting that these requirements 'impact exports' and restrict sales of high-performance products. While both address government trade regulations, MU focuses on tariff-induced cost increases for customers, whereas NVDA focuses on licensing restrictions limiting market access and sales capability.

sentences.text: In addition, increased tariffs imposed by the countries in which our products are sold can increase the cost of our product to our customers.

During the third quarter of fiscal year 2023, the U.S. government, or the USG, announced licensing requirements that, with certain exceptions, impact exports to China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and Russia of our A100 and H100 integrated circuits, DGX or any other systems or boards which incorporate A100 or H100 integrated circuits.

In October 2023, the USG announced new and updated licensing requirements that became effective in our fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024 for exports to China and Country Groups D1, D4, and D5 (including but not limited to Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Vietnam, but excluding Israel) of our products exceeding certain performance thresholds, including A100, A800, H100, H800, L4, L40, L40S and RTX 4090.
